title: Harness Builder Test Run
updated: Updated 2026-11-24 for the first full pre-archive run (Version 1.0, Build 1). Covers everything shipped so far, including iPad and iOS 17. Results cleared.

sections.name: First open and saving
sections.note: Start from a fresh install of the build you plan to archive.

sections.name: Canvas
sections.note: Pan, zoom, select, move. Try these on a real device with fingers, not only the Simulator.

sections.name: Plug sheet
sections.note: Load the example first (Try the example) so there are plugs with many wires.

sections.name: Add and edit plug wizard
sections.note: D9 is the data-loss safety check. Do it carefully.

sections.name: Component links
sections.note: Needs the example harnesses plus a Component harness.

sections.name: Export to PDF and PNG
sections.note: Save each file to Files or Photos and open it. Do not judge from the share sheet preview alone.

sections.name: iPad
sections.note: Run on an iPad simulator (or a real iPad), portrait and landscape.

sections.name: iOS 17, appearance and archive readiness
sections.note: K1 and K2 need an iOS 17 simulator. K9 and K10 are done in Xcode.

tests.title: Fresh install first screen
tests.steps: Delete the app, install the build, open it.
tests.expected: A blank canvas for a harness called My harness, with an Add your first plug card and a Try the example button. No reference codes or technical shorthand anywhere.

tests.title: Try the example
tests.steps: Tap Try the example.
tests.expected: Three harness tabs load (Engine, Firewall, ECU) with plugs on each trunk. Plug names are plain, with no research notes or reference codes.

tests.title: Add your first plug
tests.steps: On a fresh install tap Add your first plug.
tests.expected: The plug wizard opens on the shape picker.

tests.title: Saved across relaunch
tests.steps: Rename a plug, add a note, move a plug, then force-quit the app and reopen it.
tests.expected: Everything is exactly as you left it, on the same tab.

tests.title: Works with no network
tests.steps: Turn on Airplane Mode and use the app for a few minutes (open plugs, edit, export).
tests.expected: Everything works with no errors or spinners. The app never needs a network.

tests.title: Pan and pinch zoom
tests.steps: Pinch to zoom in and out and drag to pan.
tests.expected: Smooth and responsive. The grid moves and scales with the harness.

tests.title: Fit all
tests.steps: Zoom in and pan away, then tap Fit all.
tests.expected: The whole harness is visible with a margin on every side. No plug is clipped.

tests.title: Select a plug
tests.steps: Tap a plug.
tests.expected: The plug is outlined and the plug sheet opens at about half height with the canvas still visible above it.

tests.title: Canvas stays usable with the sheet open
tests.steps: With the sheet at half height, pan the canvas and tap a different plug.
tests.expected: Selection moves to the new plug and the sheet content swaps in place. No second sheet stacks on top.

tests.title: Move arrows
tests.steps: Select a plug and look at its outer edge. Tap the up arrow, then the down arrow.
tests.expected: Up and down arrows appear on the outer edge. Each tap moves the plug one place along the trunk. The arrow that cannot move is hidden or disabled at the ends.

tests.title: Arrows never clip
tests.steps: Select the first and the last plug, then tap Fit all.
tests.expected: The arrows are fully visible and not cut off at the screen edge.

tests.title: Tap empty canvas
tests.steps: With a plug selected tap an empty area of the canvas.
tests.expected: Record what happens (selection clears or not).

tests.title: Grid look
tests.steps: Look at the canvas background.
tests.expected: A faint grid is visible behind the harness. It is noticeable but does not compete with the plugs.

tests.title: Plug shapes
tests.steps: Scroll through the example harnesses and look at every plug.
tests.expected: Plugs have different real-looking shapes. No red dashed circles (unknown shape). A plain dashed outline for an unfinished shape is acceptable.

tests.title: Header and pinout
tests.steps: Open any plug.
tests.expected: The sheet shows the plug name and a numbered pinout. Wired pins are amber and empty pins are dashed.

tests.title: Wire list rows
tests.steps: Scroll the wire list.
tests.expected: Each wire row shows a color swatch, function, gauge text (if set) and role symbol (if set). Linked component plugs show goes to pin N.

tests.title: Select a wire
tests.steps: Tap a wire row.
tests.expected: The row is highlighted and its pin is marked in the pinout. A trace section appears below the list.

tests.title: Edit and Remove stay visible
tests.steps: Open a plug with a long wire list (for example the biggest ECU plug) and scroll the wire list.
tests.expected: Edit and Remove stay pinned at the bottom of the sheet the whole time. You never have to scroll to find them.

tests.title: Notes collapsed by default
tests.steps: Open a plug with no notes, then one with notes.
tests.expected: A Notes bar is always shown, collapsed by default.

tests.title: Add a note
tests.steps: Expand Notes on a plug with no notes, tap Add a note, type, save.
tests.expected: The note shows. Collapse and expand: it is kept.

tests.title: Edit a note
tests.steps: Tap Edit note, change the text, save, then force-quit and reopen.
tests.expected: The changed note is shown after relaunch.

tests.title: Switching plugs starts fresh
tests.steps: Open plug A, expand Notes and select a wire. Then tap plug B on the canvas.
tests.expected: Plug B opens fresh: Notes collapsed and no wire selected.

tests.title: Remove a plug
tests.steps: Tap Remove, then Cancel. Tap Remove again and confirm.
tests.expected: Cancel keeps the plug. Confirming removes it from the canvas and the sheet closes or swaps. The rest of the harness is untouched.

tests.title: Sheet sizes
tests.steps: Drag the sheet between half height and full height.
tests.expected: It moves smoothly and content stays readable at both sizes.

tests.title: Wired and spare counts
tests.steps: Open a plug with some empty pins.
tests.expected: The header shows pins, wired and spare, and the three numbers add up.

tests.title: Open the wizard
tests.steps: Tap + in the harness row under the tabs.
tests.expected: The shape picker opens showing each shape as a silhouette.

tests.title: Build a plug
tests.steps: Pick a shape, name it, set rows and pins, then for a few pins set color, stripe, shade, function, wire type, gauge, role and confidence. Tap Add.
tests.expected: The plug is added at the end of the trunk with the pins you set. If you left the name alone it is called Plug 1 (then Plug 2 and so on).

tests.title: Two-tone wire
tests.steps: Give a pin a main color plus a stripe color.
tests.expected: The wire list shows a two-tone swatch and the right color names.

tests.title: Empty pins
tests.steps: Leave some pins empty when building a plug.
tests.expected: They show as dashed empty pins and appear as Empty in the wire list.

tests.title: 60-pin plug
tests.steps: Build a plug with 60 pins (for example 6 rows of 10).
tests.expected: The editor fits the pins using small scrolling pin chips. The plug saves and shows on the canvas, small but readable when zoomed in.

tests.title: Size limits
tests.steps: Try to go past 60 pins, 6 rows or 20 pins per row.
tests.expected: The steppers stop at the limit. No crash and no oversized plug.

tests.title: Edit has the same fields
tests.steps: Select a plug, tap Edit, change the shape, rows, pins and name, then save.
tests.expected: Everything you can set when creating can be changed in Edit, and the plug updates.

tests.title: Edit opens on the selected wire
tests.steps: Select a wire (say pin 5) in the plug sheet, then tap Edit.
tests.expected: The editor opens already on pin 5. You do not have to find it again.

tests.title: Data-loss warning
tests.steps: Edit a plug that has pins with a color or function set. Reduce the pins (or change the shape) so those pins would be deleted. Tap save. Then cancel. Repeat and confirm.
tests.expected: A red warning shows in the editor. A Data will be lost alert says how many wired pins would be deleted. Cancel keeps all data. Confirming deletes exactly that many.

tests.title: Changing shape keeps pins in order
tests.steps: Edit a plug with the same pin count and change only its shape.
tests.expected: Pins keep their order and settings and no data-loss warning appears.

tests.title: Discard confirmation
tests.steps: In the wizard make a change, then swipe the sheet down. Then tap Cancel.
tests.expected: Swiping down does nothing while there are unsaved changes (the sheet stays open). Cancel asks before discarding, and Keep editing returns to the editor with your changes.

tests.title: Imported layout survives a small edit
tests.steps: Edit an example plug, change only one pin's function, save.
tests.expected: The plug's row layout is unchanged from before.

tests.title: New tab
tests.steps: Tap the dashed New tab.
tests.expected: The Add a harness sheet opens.

tests.title: Create a blank harness
tests.steps: Tap Create a harness.
tests.expected: A new tab and an empty canvas appear. Adding a plug works.

tests.title: Start from a template
tests.steps: Add each of Engine, Firewall and ECU from templates.
tests.expected: Each creates an editable copy with plugs. You can edit plugs, pins and names.

tests.title: Repeat a template
tests.steps: Add the Component template twice. Then open Add a harness again and look at Engine, Firewall and ECU once each has been added.
tests.expected: Component can be added repeatedly. Engine, Firewall and ECU can only be added once: they show Already added and are grayed out.

tests.title: Rename a harness
tests.steps: Tap the three-dot menu, rename, save.
tests.expected: The tab title updates and survives a relaunch.

tests.title: Delete a harness warning
tests.steps: Tap the three-dot menu and choose delete on a harness with plugs, wires and links. Cancel. Then delete and confirm.
tests.expected: The alert lists how many plugs, wires and links would be lost. Cancel keeps everything. Confirming removes the tab.

tests.title: Delete the only harness
tests.steps: Delete every harness.
tests.expected: The app shows a sensible first-open state (no crash).

tests.title: Export entry in the menu
tests.steps: Open the three-dot menu.
tests.expected: There is an Export as PDF or image button.

tests.title: Switching tabs
tests.steps: Switch between several harness tabs quickly.
tests.expected: Each shows its own plugs. No stale selection or stuck sheet.

tests.title: Check this harness
tests.steps: Open the harness menu and tap Check this harness on a harness with a missing color, an unlabeled wire and an empty plug.
tests.expected: The sheet lists likely mistakes first, then things worth a look. Tapping an item closes the sheet and selects that plug.

tests.title: Check finds nothing
tests.steps: Run Check this harness on a harness where every wire has a color and label.
tests.expected: It says nothing looks wrong.

tests.title: Component harness
tests.steps: Add the Component template and open its plug.
tests.expected: The plug sheet has a link section for linking to a plug on another harness.

tests.title: Link picker
tests.steps: Tap to link and look at the list.
tests.expected: It lists plugs on the other harnesses (not the component's own).

tests.title: Linked state
tests.steps: Pick a plug to link to.
tests.expected: A Linked to card shows the target. Wires that match show goes to pin N.

tests.title: Jump both ways
tests.steps: Tap the Linked to card. On the target plug, tap the Linked component card.
tests.expected: The first tap switches to the target harness and plug. The second takes you back to the component.

tests.title: Change link and Unlink
tests.steps: Tap Change link and choose another plug. Then Unlink.
tests.expected: Change link updates the card. Unlink removes it and the goes to pin N notes.

tests.title: No link on normal harnesses
tests.steps: Open a plug in the Engine harness.
tests.expected: There is no link section there (links belong to component harnesses).

tests.title: Delete the link target
tests.steps: Remove the plug a component is linked to, then open the component plug.
tests.expected: No crash. The link is no longer shown. (There is no warning yet.)

tests.title: Same wire continues at
tests.steps: With the example loaded select a wire that appears on another plug.
tests.expected: The trace section lists Same wire continues at with the plug and pin.

tests.title: Does the same job in
tests.steps: Select a wire with the same job in another harness.
tests.expected: The section Does the same job in lists the other harness's plug and pin.

tests.title: Whole-plug match
tests.steps: Open a plug that matches another plug as a whole but has no wire-level match.
tests.expected: A section This plug as a whole matches lists it.

tests.title: Connected plugs outlined
tests.steps: Select a wire with matches and look at the canvas.
tests.expected: The connected plugs are outlined, visibly different from the selected plug.

tests.title: Jump and zoom
tests.steps: Tap a result in the trace section.
tests.expected: The app switches harness if needed, selects that plug, and pans and zooms so it is clearly visible above the sheet.

tests.title: Wires you build (not connected)
tests.steps: Build a plug yourself and select one of its wires.
tests.expected: The trace section says this wire isn't connected to another plug yet and points to Connects to.

tests.title: Empty pin
tests.steps: Select an empty pin in the pinout.
tests.expected: No crash and no trace results.

tests.title: Connect two wires you built
tests.steps: Build two plugs. Edit the second, pick a wire, tap Connect to a pin, choose the first plug and one of its wires, then save.
tests.expected: Connects to shows the other plug and pin before saving. After saving, selecting that wire lists Same wire continues at with the other plug and pin.

tests.title: Connection works from the other end
tests.steps: Open the first plug from G8 and select the wire you connected to.
tests.expected: Same wire continues at lists the second plug and pin. Tapping it jumps there. The connected plug is outlined on the canvas.

tests.title: Connect across harnesses
tests.steps: Edit a plug on one harness and connect a wire to a pin on a plug on another harness.
tests.expected: The picker lists plugs from every harness. After saving, the trace section jumps to the other harness.

tests.title: Clear a connection
tests.steps: Edit the wire from G8 and tap Clear, then save.
tests.expected: Connects to is empty and the wire shows no Same wire continues at. The other plug keeps working.

tests.title: Connect then cancel
tests.steps: Connect a wire to another plug in the wizard, then Cancel and discard.
tests.expected: Nothing is saved on either plug.

tests.title: Set a gauge
tests.steps: Edit a wire, set the gauge to 18, save.
tests.expected: The wire list shows 18 AWG as text. There is no visual indicator for gauge anywhere else.

tests.title: Gauge is optional
tests.steps: Leave the gauge empty on a wire.
tests.expected: No gauge text appears for that wire.

tests.title: Set a role
tests.steps: Edit a wire and set role to hot, then signal, then ground.
tests.expected: A role symbol shows in the wire list and the pinout for each.

tests.title: Roles toggle defaults off
tests.steps: Force-quit and reopen the app. Look at the Roles toggle in the header.
tests.expected: It is off. The canvas pins show no role symbols.

tests.title: Roles toggle on and off
tests.steps: Turn the Roles toggle on, then off.
tests.expected: On: symbols show beside pins that have a role. Off: they disappear.

tests.title: Roles are never guessed
tests.steps: Build a plug without setting any role.
tests.expected: No pin gets a role symbol automatically.

tests.title: Roles in the export drawing
tests.steps: Turn Roles on and export a harness with roles set.
tests.expected: Record whether role symbols appear on the exported drawing.

tests.title: Export sheet
tests.steps: Tap the three-dot menu, then Export as PDF or image.
tests.expected: A sheet offers this harness or all harnesses, PDF or PNG, and a wire table toggle that is on by default.

tests.title: PDF of this harness
tests.steps: Choose this harness and PDF, create the file, save it to Files and open it.
tests.expected: Page 1 is a cover page with the harness name and the whole drawing. The following pages are US Letter wire tables.

tests.title: PDF of all harnesses
tests.steps: Choose all harnesses and PDF.
tests.expected: One PDF with a cover page per harness (each followed by its tables).

tests.title: Table content
tests.steps: Read the wire tables.
tests.expected: Columns: pin, color swatch and name, function, gauge, wire type, and how sure. Empty pins show Empty. A plug's title never sits alone at the bottom of a page.

tests.title: PNG export
tests.steps: Choose PNG and save to Photos.
tests.expected: One tall image per harness: the drawing on top, the table below. Text is readable when zoomed.

tests.title: Table off
tests.steps: Turn the wire table toggle off and export PDF and PNG.
tests.expected: PDF has only the cover pages. PNG has only the drawing.

tests.title: Large harness
tests.steps: Export a harness with several 60-pin plugs (or a very long harness) as PDF and as PNG.
tests.expected: Both succeed with no crash or blank output. A very long PNG is made at a lower resolution instead of failing.

tests.title: Print the PDF
tests.steps: From the share sheet choose Print.
tests.expected: The print preview shows all pages.

tests.title: Dark background
tests.steps: Look at an exported page.
tests.expected: The export uses the app's dark background, which uses a lot of ink if printed. A white-background print option may be added later.

tests.title: Nothing private in the export
tests.steps: Export the example harnesses and read the PDF.
tests.expected: No reference codes, research notes or personal names appear.

tests.title: CSV wire list
tests.steps: Export as CSV for This harness, then All harnesses. Open the file in Numbers, Excel or Sheets.
tests.expected: One row per wire with plug, pin, color, function, gauge, type and Connects to. Commas and quotes in names do not break the columns.

tests.title: Print-friendly export
tests.steps: Export a PDF and a PNG with Print-friendly on, then print the PDF or view it.
tests.expected: White page, dark text, plain white plugs. Everything is readable and uses little ink. With it off, the dark export is unchanged.

tests.title: iPad layout
tests.steps: Run on an iPad simulator in portrait. Open the app and the example.
tests.expected: The header, tabs and first-open card look sensible on the wide screen. Nothing is stretched or lopsided.

tests.title: Sheet on iPad
tests.steps: Tap a plug.
tests.expected: Record how the plug sheet appears (bottom sheet or floating panel). The canvas remains tappable and pannable with it open.

tests.title: Landscape
tests.steps: Rotate the iPad to landscape and back.
tests.expected: The harness and sheet stay usable. Fit all works in both orientations.

tests.title: Wizard on iPad
tests.steps: Open the wizard and build a plug.
tests.expected: Pin editing, steppers and scrolling work. Nothing is cut off.

tests.title: Export on iPad
tests.steps: Export a PDF.
tests.expected: The share sheet appears as a popover and does not crash.

tests.title: iOS 17 launch and screens
tests.steps: Run on an iOS 17 simulator and visit every screen: canvas, plug sheet, wizard, Add a harness, harness menu, link picker, export.
tests.expected: No crash and everything is usable.

tests.title: Sheets on iOS 17
tests.steps: On iOS 17 tap a plug and use the canvas while the sheet is at half height.
tests.expected: The canvas stays interactive behind the sheet, as on newer iOS.

tests.title: iOS 26 look
tests.steps: On an iOS 26 device or simulator open the sheets and buttons.
tests.expected: System controls use the new look. The custom canvas drawing looks the same as on iOS 17.

tests.title: Light icon
tests.steps: Set the device to Light appearance and look at the home screen.
tests.expected: The light icon shows: a plug on a pale grid with the outline clearly visible.

tests.title: Dark icon
tests.steps: Set the device to Dark appearance.
tests.expected: The dark icon shows: a plug on a dark grid with the outline clearly visible.

tests.title: Tinted icon
tests.steps: Long-press the home screen, tap Customize, choose Tinted.
tests.expected: A grayscale icon tinted with the chosen color. Still recognizable.

tests.title: App name
tests.steps: Look at the name under the icon.
tests.expected: Harness Builder, not truncated.

tests.title: Appearance follows the phone
tests.steps: Open Settings and confirm Appearance is System. Switch the device between Light and Dark.
tests.expected: The app follows the device setting right away. Nothing becomes unreadable.

tests.title: Version and build numbers
tests.steps: In Xcode open the target's General tab.
tests.expected: Version and Build are what you intend to archive and match the git tag you will create (ios-v1.0-build1 for the first upload).

tests.title: Archive and validate
tests.steps: Product, Archive, then Validate App in the Organizer.
tests.expected: The archive succeeds and validation reports no errors (icon has no transparency, correct sizes, bundle id, category).

tests.title: Real device gestures
tests.steps: On a real iPhone use pinch, pan, tap and drag the sheet with your fingers.
tests.expected: Gestures feel responsive and do not fight each other.

tests.title: Performance
tests.steps: Load all example harnesses and pan and zoom on the oldest device you have.
tests.expected: No noticeable lag or heat.

tests.title: Settings opens
tests.steps: Tap the gear at the left of the tab row.
tests.expected: The Settings sheet shows Appearance, Build with AI (coming soon) and About with the version. Done closes it.

tests.title: Choose Light or Dark
tests.steps: In Settings choose Light, then Dark, then System. Force-quit and reopen the app.
tests.expected: The app switches each time and keeps your choice after relaunch.

tests.title: Light mode, every screen
tests.steps: Set Light. Visit the canvas, plug sheet, wizard (every step), Add a harness, harness menu, link picker, wire picker, export sheet and Settings.
tests.expected: Every screen is readable: text, buttons, pin colors, the red data-loss warning, selection outlines. Plugs are gray with a dark outline.

tests.title: Dark mode unchanged
tests.steps: Set Dark and visit the same screens.
tests.expected: It looks as it did before this change.

tests.title: Exports ignore the appearance
tests.steps: In Light mode export a PDF and a PNG.
tests.expected: The files look the same as when exported in Dark mode.

tests.title: Every change survives relaunch
tests.steps: Add a plug, edit pins, move a plug, add a link, add a note, delete a plug. Force-quit after each and reopen.
tests.expected: Each change is still there after relaunch.

tests.title: Update over an older build
tests.steps: If you have a build from before gauge and role existed, install this build over it.
tests.expected: The app opens with your old data intact and no crash.

tests.title: Empty states
tests.steps: Remove every plug from a harness, then delete all harnesses.
tests.expected: Sensible empty screens and no crash.

tests.title: Rapid taps
tests.steps: Quickly tap plug, arrows, Edit, Cancel and the harness menu in sequence.
tests.expected: No stuck or stacked sheets. You can always dismiss and carry on.

tests.title: Long names
tests.steps: Give a plug and a harness very long names.
tests.expected: Text truncates or wraps and the layout does not break.

tests.title: Special characters
tests.steps: Use emoji, quotes and non-English letters in names, functions and notes.
tests.expected: They save, display and export correctly.

tests.title: Back up
tests.steps: In Settings tap Back up to Files or share and save the file to Files.
tests.expected: A file named Harness Builder backup with today's date is saved.

tests.title: Restore
tests.steps: Change something in the app. In Settings tap Restore from a backup and choose the file from L7. Confirm.
tests.expected: A warning shows the number of harnesses and plugs. After confirming, the app matches the backup.

tests.title: Restore the wrong file
tests.steps: In Settings tap Restore and choose a file that is not a backup (a photo or a PDF).
tests.expected: A clear message says it isn't a Harness Builder backup, and nothing changes.
